installation.note: passwd is a core system command available on all Linux systems

overview.summary: passwd changes a user's password. Regular users can change only their own password; root can change any user's password and also lock/unlock accounts or set expiry. It updates the shadow password database.
when_to_use: As root: change or lock another user's password
Set or expire passwords for user accounts

syntax.description: Without USERNAME, passwd changes the current user's password. Root can specify USERNAME.

options.use_case: Disable an account without deleting it

options.description: Force password expiry (user must change at next login)
options.use_case: Force a user to set a new password

options.description: Delete the user's password (allow passwordless login; use with caution)
options.use_case: Remove password (risky; often for special accounts)

examples.use_case: Admin setting or resetting a user password
